req.title: Login required for update
req.statement: The system shall redirect anonymous users to /auth/login when they attempt GET /<id>/update.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-013 requires that anonymous (unauthenticated) users attempting GET /<id>/update are redirected to /auth/login. Three test cases are designed: (1) positive — an authenticated user can access the update page (status 200), confirming the redirect only fires for anonymous users; (2) negative — an anonymous user gets a 302 redirect to /auth/login (the primary requirement); (3) boundary — the redirect target URL is exactly '/auth/login' (not a prefix, not a superset), catching constant-mutation and string-mutation operators. Each test uses exact-value assertions to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_anonymous_get_update_redirects_to_login
preconditions: Application is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database is pre-loaded with fixture data (post id=1 exists)
No user is logged in (anonymous session)
actions: Send GET /1/update without any session cookie
expected: HTTP response status code is exactly 302
trace: R-FLASKR-013: anonymous GET /<id>/update must redirect to /auth/login
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

def test_anonymous_get_update_redirects_to_login():
    r = client.get('/1/update')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

test_anonymous_get_update_redirects_to_login()

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

def test_authenticated_user_can_access_update_page():
    login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert login_r.status_code == 302
    r = client.get('/1/update')
    assert r.status_code == 200

test_authenticated_user_can_access_update_page()

tests.name: test_anonymous_redirect_location_is_exactly_auth_login
preconditions: Application is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database is pre-loaded with fixture data (post id=1 exists)
actions: Send GET /1/update without any session cookie
Inspect the exact value of the Location header
expected: Location header equals '/auth/login' exactly — not '/auth/login/', not '/login', not any other string
trace: R-FLASKR-013: redirect destination must be exactly /auth/login (catches constant/string mutations in url_for('auth.login'))
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

def test_anonymous_redirect_location_is_exactly_auth_login():
    r = client.get('/1/update')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    location = r.headers['Location']
    assert location == '/auth/login'
    assert location != '/auth/login/'
    assert location != '/login'
    assert location != '/auth/register'

test_anonymous_redirect_location_is_exactly_auth_login()

tests.name: test_anonymous_get_update_does_not_return_200
preconditions: Application is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database is pre-loaded with fixture data (post id=1 exists)
actions: Send GET /1/update without any session cookie
Assert the response is NOT a success (not 200)
expected: Status code is 302, confirming the request was not served as a success
Response body does not contain the update form HTML
trace: R-FLASKR-013: anonymous access must never yield a 200 — catches mutations that remove the login_required decorator

from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

def test_anonymous_get_update_follow_redirect_lands_on_login_page():
